how.title: How I work
how.lead: Five phases shared by every way of working: what you see in each and what I need from you.

phases.discover: I learn what problem the product solves, for whom and what goes into the first version.
phases.design: I sketch screens and flows and test them with you before writing code.
phases.build: I build in short deliveries you can try on your phone or in a preview.
phases.publish: I ship the app to the stores and the site to its domain, with analytics and backups.
phases.maintain: I fix, update and improve after launch, with an agreed plan.

how.more: See how I work, with examples

hub.q1: Do you work remotely or do I need to be in Madrid?
hub.a1: I work remotely with clients across Spain and abroad. When needed, I can travel to one-off meetings in Madrid.
hub.q2: Do you invoice as a self-employed freelancer, or can I hire you through a consultancy?
hub.a2: I am not registered as self-employed yet and can invoice one-off work. If you need to hire me through a consultancy or company, we work it out case by case and put it in writing before starting.
hub.q3: Which languages can I write to you in?
hub.a3: Spanish and English. Code documentation and commit messages are in English.
hub.q4: How long do you take to reply?
hub.a4: I answer every enquiry within {responseTime}, usually sooner. If it is urgent, say so in the message.
hub.q5: Will you sign a non-disclosure agreement (NDA)?
hub.a5: Yes, I can sign one before you tell me anything sensitive, with your template or a standard one.
hub.q6: How much working-hours overlap do you have with my team?
hub.a6: I work on Madrid hours and coordinate with teams in other time zones. Tell me when you need to talk and I will tell you which window I can cover.
hub.q7: What if I do not like the result?
hub.a7: I work in short deliveries you see before I go on, so the course is corrected early and not at the end. If it still does not fit, we talk it through and decide together how to close it.

freelance.q1: Is there a minimum number of hours?
freelance.a1: There is no fixed minimum. For very small tasks we agree a block of hours or a per-task price before starting.
freelance.q2: Which suits me better, hourly or per task?
freelance.a2: Per task if the scope is clear and you want a fixed price. Hourly if the scope may change or is exploratory.
freelance.a3: I work in short deliveries you can try, and I share each step without waiting for the end.
freelance.q4: What happens if the scope grows?
freelance.a4: We agree it before going on: I explain what changes in time and cost, and you decide whether to include it or leave it for another task.
freelance.q5: Will you sign an NDA before seeing my code?
freelance.a5: Yes, I can sign one before you give me access to anything sensitive. If you already have a template, send it over and I will review it.
freelance.q6: How much working-hours overlap do you offer if I go by the hour?
freelance.a6: I work on Madrid hours and can overlap with you in a fixed window for questions and reviews.

offers.q1: How much does a mobile app cost?
offers.a1: It depends on the tier and the extras. Each tier has a "from" price and, after talking to you, I give you a fixed quote with a delivery date.
offers.a2: Design, development and release. The exact list for each tier is in the comparison and is confirmed in writing before starting.
offers.q3: Is publishing to the stores included?
offers.a3: Yes. App tiers include publishing to the App Store and Google Play with your accounts, and web tiers include the domain and hosting.
offers.q4: Is there a warranty and maintenance after launch?
offers.a4: I fix bugs in the agreed scope for thirty days after delivery at no cost. After that, maintenance is an optional monthly plan in three sizes.
offers.q5: What do I need to provide?
offers.a5: The texts, the images and the business decisions. I tell you what I need in each phase and when, so delivery is not held up.
offers.q6: What if I want something the tier does not have?
offers.a6: We talk before touching it: I explain what changes in time and cost, and you decide whether to add it as an extra or leave it out.
offers.q7: What if you fall ill or disappear?
offers.a7: The repository, the domain, the stores and the services are in your name from day one, and I leave documentation so another developer can carry on without me. If something happened to me I would tell you right away and the timeline would be readjusted with you.
offers.a8: Yes. The code and the design of the project are yours, and the store and domain accounts are in your name. The transfer of rights is put in writing in the proposal.
offers.a9: Yes. Payment is split into three phases: 40% at the start, 40% when the design is delivered and 20% on launch. Each phase is confirmed in writing in the proposal.
offers.q10: What happens if I want to change something halfway through the project?
offers.a10: It can be done. Before touching it I explain what changes in timeline and cost, and I only apply it if you approve it in writing. If you approve it, it comes with its own timeline.

problems.title: How I solve problems
problems.lead: Three real cases from this very site: the problem, the decision I made and what came out of it.

csp.title: A strict CSP on Cloudflare Workers
csp.problem: I wanted a content security policy without “unsafe-inline” for scripts, on a site rendered at the edge, where there is no traditional server to hand out nonces.
csp.decision: I generate a different nonce on every request in the Next proxy, send it in the header and pass it to every script, JSON-LD included. “strict-dynamic” lets those trusted scripts load the rest.
csp.result: A script without a nonce does not run. An end-to-end test watches the security headers on every change.

motion.title: Accessible motion without the JavaScript cost
motion.problem: Motion makes an interface feel cared for, but it makes people who ask for less animation dizzy and is usually paid for in kilobytes of JavaScript.
motion.decision: Almost all motion is native CSS, with curves and durations defined as tokens. A single reduced-motion rule switches off transitions and animations across the site.
motion.result: The hero walks through the five phases in CSS and, with reduced motion, stays still on “Publish”. Changing a curve happens in one place.

recommender.title: A rule-based recommender, not an AI
recommender.problem: Choosing between web and app tiers and twelve extras is overwhelming. A generative chatbot would be slow, cost money per query and could make up a price.
recommender.decision: Six questions and a pure function that returns the offer and the extras. The state lives in the URL and Nexo guides with a script, without generating free text.
recommender.result: Same answers, same recommendation; no cost per query, linkable and covered by unit tests.

tech.title: Technology and architecture
tech.lead: This site is my case study: it runs at the edge, stores data with row-level permissions and checks itself before every merge.

diagram.label: Architecture of this site
diagram.caption: Simplified architecture: who uses the site, where it runs and where the data lives.
diagram.description: Diagram that reads left to right, or top to bottom on mobile. The browser connects to the Next 16 application, which runs on Cloudflare Workers; continuous integration on GitHub Actions checks it before it is published. The application reads and writes data in Supabase, where Postgres enforces row-level security and authentication, storage and realtime are provided.

browser.name: Browser
browser.detail: The public site and the private areas, each with its own role.

workers.name: Next 16 on Cloudflare Workers
workers.detail: Edge rendering with OpenNext, nonce-based CSP and rate limiting.

ci.name: CI on GitHub Actions
ci.detail: Lint, types, tests, build, e2e with axe and pgTAP against every migration on each pull request.

postgres.name: Supabase Postgres
postgres.detail: RLS on every table with user data and a schema changed only by migrations.

services.name: Auth, Storage and Realtime
services.detail: Email OTP, TOTP for staff and signed URLs.

next.title: Next 16 on Cloudflare Workers
next.text: Server Components by default, JavaScript only where needed and rendering close to the user.

supabase.title: Supabase with RLS
supabase.text: Postgres with row-level permissions on every table: the browser never has more access than it should.

typescript.title: Strict TypeScript
typescript.text: Types inferred from zod schemas at every boundary: whatever comes in is validated before it is used.

tests.title: Tests in four layers
tests.text: Unit, end-to-end with Playwright, accessibility with axe and pgTAP for the database policies.

ci.title: Continuous integration
ci.text: Every change to this site has gone in through a pull request, and each one runs lint, types, tests, build and the database tests, with a preview to review it.

quality.title: Standards I meet
quality.lead: The ones I demand of this site and bring to every project.

accessibility.title: WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility
accessibility.text: Keyboard, visible focus and contrast in every component. If axe finds a violation, continuous integration fails.

performance.title: Performance budget
performance.text: LCP under 2.5 s, INP under 200 ms, CLS under 0.1 and less than 150 KB of JavaScript on the home page.

security.title: Security from day one
security.text: Nonce-based CSP, strict headers, RLS on every table, Turnstile and rate limiting on public forms.

code.title: Code without comments
code.text: The why lives in clear names, in the commit or in a written decision. The linter enforces it.

tokens.title: Design tokens
tokens.text: One source for colour, spacing and motion. Components only use variables and contrast is checked in CI.

story.title: My story
story.p1: I'm a full stack developer and my specialty is React Native: one codebase for iOS and Android, with the web and the server built with the same tools and the same language.
story.p2: I like to own a product from start to finish: the app people see, the website that presents it and the data behind it. I would rather ship something small that works and improve it in the open than disappear for months and present a closed box.
story.p3: I live in Madrid and work with teams and clients across Spain and remotely. Native Spanish and professional English.
